title: Tamsin and the Harbor
premise: In 1890s harbor city of Greywater, Tamsin Pemberton—daughter of a drowned pearl diver, indentured to the Meridian Trading Company since age nine—has survived by being useful and unseen. When a weathered stranger named Callum arrives bearing letters in her father's unmistakable hand, she learns the man she mourned may have faked his death to escape the Company's debts, and that Meridian's founders built their fortune on pearls salvaged from divers they let die. Racing a company historian who is burning the ledgers, Tamsin must gather testimony from the harbor's outcasts—the divers, widows, and smugglers who remember—to force the truth into the public record before the archive closes forever. In the end she trades her own anonymity for justice: her father is dead after all, but the Company's crimes are entered into the civic record, and the harbor community that raised her claims her as family.
about_author: Ivo Marchetti is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers and diver compensation claims along the northern coast. Their fiction draws on the half-erased lives found in marginalia, water-stained paybooks, and the silences between official entries.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Hands
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A day in the life of an indentured clerk at Meridian Trading: mending nets of paperwork, hiding her literacy, memorizing what she isn't supposed to read. Establishes her invisibility strategy and the harbor's rhythms. Emotional beat: quiet pride in competence shadowed by the ache of belonging to no one.

chapters.title: Letters for a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A stranger, Callum Reeve, arrives at the counting house asking after Wendell Pemberton—a dead pearl diver—and produces letters in a handwriting Tamsin knows better than her own. She says nothing, but copies the return address by lamplight. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of her carefully ordered world.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Owe
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with a flashback to her father's last dive. She begins quietly investigating the debt ledger that bound her family, discovering entries altered in a supervisor's hand. First hint that Meridian falsified dive records. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Historian's Apprentice
chapters.summary: POV shift to Elias Voss, the young company historian hired to write Meridian's official centenary history. He notices gaps in the archives—pages razored out—and his mentor warns him curiosity is a career-ending disease. Emotional beat: uneasy complicity; he wants truth but loves his position more, for now.

chapters.title: Salt and Widow's Bread
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She visits Maren Ostrow, a diver's widow who runs a boarding house, testing whether anyone else received letters from the 'dead.' Maren reveals three other families got them—and were paid to stay silent. Emotional beat: the first fragile alliance; Tamsin realizes she isn't alone.

chapters.title: Callum's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts Callum on the pier at night. He admits he was her father's dive partner, that Wendell staged his death to escape a debt trap, and that he promised to find 'the girl' if things went wrong. He won't say what went wrong. Emotional beat: anger and longing tangled together.

chapters.title: The Burning Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ordered to prepare archives for destruction ahead of a merger, Elias pockets one ledger page on impulse—a diver fatality list with names struck through. He glimpses 'W. Pemberton' twice. Emotional beat: the moment complicity tips toward conscience.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cross-referencing the fatality list against payroll books hidden in the loft, she finds a pattern: divers who died were those whose salvage exceeded their debts. The Company profited from their deaths. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into cold, clarifying fury.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Callum seek out Old Brannick, a retired smuggler who ran contraband past Meridian's inspectors for decades. His account corroborates the salvage-theft pattern—but he'll only testify if protected. Emotional beat: hope complicated by the cost of asking people to risk everything.

chapters.title: Supervisor Crane Takes Notice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Her absences are noticed by Supervisor Crane, who offers her a promotion—freedom papers in exchange for loyalty and silence about 'old accounts.' She must smile and accept time to decide. Emotional beat: terror beneath a compliant mask; the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: Maren's Room Above the Water
chapters.summary: POV alternates briefly among the widows at Maren's boarding house as they compare memories of their husbands' final dives. A collective portrait emerges of a rigged system. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing around shared loss and shared resolve.

chapters.title: Elias Comes Asking
chapters.summary: Elias, following his pocketed page, tracks down Tamsin under pretense of routine records verification. Each recognizes the other's game. They strike an uneasy truce: he wants the true history; she wants it on the record. Emotional beat: wary mutual respect across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Night the Archive Burned Early
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Fire guts the Meridian record annex weeks ahead of schedule. Tamsin and Callum salvage a water-damaged strongbox of original dive contracts from the flooded cellar before Crane's men arrive. Emotional beat: desperate triumph turning to dread—they now hold evidence worth killing for.

chapters.title: Crane's Question
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, interrogation scene. Crane, knowing the strongbox is gone, gives Tamsin until the merger signing to return it—or be charged with theft and lose any claim to freedom. Emotional beat: isolation and fear; even allies could be compromised.

chapters.title: What Callum Never Said
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Confession chapter: Wendell didn't escape—he was dying of diver's lung and staged his death so his salvage claims would fund Tamsin's eventual freedom. The letters were his insurance. Callum has been protecting a promise, not a living man. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; grief renewed and transformed.

chapters.title: The Widows' Council
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At Maren's, the community votes: testify publicly at the merger hearing despite risks. Brannick agrees, the widows agree, and Elias commits to entering their statements into the civic record rather than the company archive. Emotional beat: courage as a collective act; Tamsin finally belongs.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Counting House
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A trusted ally—junior clerk Fenwick, whom she'd confided in—sells the plan to Crane for his own freedom papers. The strongbox is seized; Callum is arrested on old smuggling charges. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting, and the temptation to run.

chapters.title: The Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. With the physical evidence gone, she gambles on memory: dozens of harbor folk arrive unbidden at the hearing, each carrying fragments—paybook stubs, tally marks tattooed on forearms, songs encoding dive counts. Emotional beat: rising defiance; the archive burns but the harbor does not forget.

chapters.title: Hearing Day
chapters.summary: Climax. Tamsin testifies, reading her father's final letter aloud and entering the reconstructed record through Elias, who defies his employers on the stand. Crane's counterattack collapses when Fenwick, shamed, recants and confirms the theft order. Emotional beat: terror becoming voice; the truth spoken into permanence.

chapters.title: The Price of Paper
chapters.summary: Aftermath of the hearing. Meridian settles to avoid scandal; the divers' families receive restitution; Crane resigns. But Tamsin's own indenture is technically still valid—a last clause. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by unfinished business.

chapters.title: Freedom Papers
chapters.summary: Resolution. Elias, now keeper of the new civic archive, finds the original manumission clause her father purchased with his final salvage—and files it himself. Tamsin signs her own name, full and legible, for the first time. Emotional beat: identity claimed; inheritance redefined as truth instead of debt.

chapters.title: Tamsin of the Harbor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Tamsin's POV. One year later: she works as the archive's first lay records-keeper, teaching harbor children to read ledgers. Callum stays; Maren's house is full; her father's letter hangs framed above the desk. Emotional beat: peace earned, family chosen, a name that finally fits.
